tasks.title: Ground takes height from lidar, not the live world surface
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-27 from the SUSU void review. Rule (owner): lidar is the source of truth for ground height; the live game surface may only inform transitional choices (e.g. matching paving between a feature and ground, either built first), never height. Cause class: Translation. ground_layer.free_columns reads the live surface via surface_y although the module docstring says HOW HIGH is composite lidar; so a wrong ghost baseline is repainted, not corrected. Observed: columns where live is 36-39 and lidar ground is 46-50 stayed low after a ground rerun; some were footprint columns (never touched), one a free column at a cell edge (level_pits rim only sees columns inside the cell). Deliver: ground heights come from lidar_heightmap base (reference world); pits/spikes logic follows from comparing live to lidar rather than live to its neighbours; consider filling under footprint wall bases to lidar ground; rim lookups read across cell edges. Proof: unit test on MemoryBlocks where live dips below lidar and ground raises to lidar, footprint columns and live-only paving hints unchanged. Files: lib/layers/ground_layer.py, lib/layers/test_ground_layer.py, rules/evidence-order.md if it needs the live-surface carve-out wording. Helps: all layered ground, any world on a lidar ghost baseline.
